title: No deceit in the Saviour’s coming
source_text: Ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν διδότωσαν τῷ Κέλσῳ ὅτι οὐ μεταβάλλει μὲν, ποιεῖ δὲ τοὺς ὁρῶντας δοκεῖν αὐτὸν μεταβεβληκέναι· ἡμεῖς, δὲ πειθόμενοι οι᾿ δόκησιν ἀλλ᾿ ἀλήθειαν εἶναι καὶ ἐνάργειαν κατὰ τὴν Ἰησοῦ εἰς ἀνθρώπους ἐπιδημίαν, οὐχ ὑποκείμεθα τῇ Κέλσου κατηγορίᾳ. ὅμως δ᾿ ἀπολογησόμεθα ὅτι οὐ φῂς, ὦ Κέλσε, ὡς ἐν φαρμάκου μοίρᾳ ποτὲ δίδοται χρῆσθαι τῷ πλανᾶν καὶ τῷ ψεύδεσθαι; τί οὖν ἄτοπον, εἰ τοιοῦτόν τι ἔμελλε σῴζειν, τοιοῦτόν τι γεγονέναι; καὶ γάρ τινες τῶν λόγων τὰ τοιαδὶ ἤθη κατὰ τὸ ψεῦδος μᾶλλον λεγόμενοι ἐπιστρέφουσιν, ὥσπερ καὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν ποτε λόγοι τοιοίδε πρὸς τοὺς κάμνοντας. ἤπερ κατὰ τὸ ἀληθές. ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν περὶ ἑτέρων ἀπολελογήσθω ἡμῖν. καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἄτοπόν ἐστι τὸν ἰώμενον φίλους νοσοῦντας ἰάσασθαι τὸ φίλον τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος τοῖς τοιοῖσδε, οἷς οὐκ ἄν τις χρήσαιτο προηγουμένως ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ περιστάσεως. καὶ μεμηνὸς δὲ τὸ γένος τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἔδει θεραπευθῆναι διὰ μεθόδων, ὧν ἑώρα ὁ λόγος χρησίμων τοῖς μεμηνόσιν, ἵνα σωφρονήσωσι. φησὶ δ᾿ ὅτι καὶ τὰ τοιάδε τις ποιεῖ πρὸς ἐχθροὺς, κίνδυνον ἐκφυγεῖν προμηθούμενος. οὐ φοβεῖται δέ τινας ὁ θεὸς, ἵνα πλανήσας τοὺς ἐπιβουλεύοντας κίνδυνον διαφύγῃ. πάντῃ δὲ περισσὸν καὶ ἄλογον ἀπολογήσασθαι πρὸς τὸ ὑπ᾿ οὐδενὸς περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν λεγόμενον. προείρηται δ᾿ εἰς τὴν περὶ ἑτέρων ἡμῖν ἀπολογίαν πρὸς τὸ οὔτε δὲ νοσῶν ἢ μεμηνὼς οὐδεὶς φίλος τῷ θεῷ· ὁ γὰρ ἀπολογησάμενός φησιν οὐχ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἤδη φίλων νοσούντων ἢ μεμηνότων τὴν τοιάνδε οἰκονομίαν γίνεσθαι ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὲρ τῶν διὰ νόσον τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ ἔκστασιν τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν λογισμοῦ ἔτι ἐχθρῶν. ἵνα γένωνται φίλοι τῷ θεῷ. καὶ γὰρ σαφῶς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτωλῶν λέγεται πάντα ἀναδεδέχθαι ὁ Ἰησοῦς. ἵν᾿ αὐτοὺς „ἀπαλλάξῃ“ τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ ποιήσῃ „δικαίους.“
pass_a_gloss: Let others then grant (διδότωσαν) Celsus that he does not change, but makes the seers think (δοκεῖν) him to have changed; but we, persuaded (πειθόμενοι) that not appearance (δόκησιν) but truth (ἀλήθειαν) and vividness/evident reality (ἐνάργειαν) was in Jesus' sojourn (ἐπιδημίαν) among men, are not liable (ὑποκείμεθα) to Celsus's accusation (κατηγορίᾳ). Yet we shall answer (ἀπολογησόμεθα): do you not say, O Celsus, that as in the part of a drug it is sometimes given/allowed (δίδοται) to use misleading and lying? What absurd then, if such a thing was going to save (σῴζειν), that such a thing happened? For some words, spoken rather according to falsehood (κατὰ τὸ ψεῦδος), turn (ἐπιστρέφουσιν) such characters (ἤθη), as also physicians' words sometimes to the sick, than according to the true (κατὰ τὸ ἀληθές). But let these be defended by us concerning others (περὶ ἑτέρων). For it is not absurd that the one healing sick friends should heal the friend/dear (φίλον) race of men with such things as one would not use principally (προηγουμένως) but from circumstance (ἐκ περιστάσεως). And the race of men, being mad, had to be treated (θεραπευθῆναι) by methods (μεθόδων) which the Word saw useful to the mad, so that they might become sound-minded (σωφρονήσωσι). He says that one does such things to enemies, providing to escape danger; but God does not fear anyone so as, misleading the plotters (ἐπιβουλεύοντας), to escape danger. Altogether superfluous (περισσόν) and unreasonable (ἄλογον) to answer what is said by no one about our Saviour. It was said before, in our defence for others, against 'no one sick or mad is friend to God': for the defender says such a dispensation (οἰκονομίαν) happens not for friends already sick or mad but for those still enemies (ἔτι ἐχθρῶν) through sickness of soul (νόσον τῆς ψυχῆς) and displacement (ἔκστασιν) of natural reasoning (τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν λογισμοῦ), so they may become friends to God. For it is clearly said that Jesus undertook (ἀναδεδέχθαι) all things for sinners (ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτωλῶν), that he might 'release (ἀπαλλάξῃ)' them from sin and make them 'righteous (δικαίους)'.
pass_b_english: Let others, then, grant Celsus that he does not change, but makes those who see him think he has changed. We, however, who are convinced that in the coming of Jesus among men there was no semblance but truth and plain reality, are not open to Celsus’s charge.

Even so, we will make this answer: Do you not say, Celsus, that it is sometimes permitted to use deceit and lying as a kind of medicine? What is absurd, then, in something of this kind having taken place, if something of this kind was going to bring salvation? For some words, when spoken falsely rather than truthfully, turn certain characters back, as do some words that physicians at times speak to the sick. But let this be our defence on behalf of others.

For it is not absurd that he who heals friends who are sick should heal the human race, which is dear to him, by such means as one would not use by preference, but because circumstances demand it. And the human race, being mad, had to be cured by methods that the Word saw were useful for the mad, so that they might come to their senses.

He says, too, that one does such things toward enemies, “when one is taking care to escape danger”. But God does not fear anyone, so as to escape danger by leading astray those who plot against him. It is wholly superfluous and unreasonable to answer what no one says about our Saviour.

As for the words “But no one who is sick or mad is a friend of God”, an answer has already been given in our defence on behalf of others. For whoever makes that defence says that such a dispensation takes place not for those who are already friends and are sick or mad, but for those who, through sickness of soul and the derangement of their natural reasoning, are still enemies (Romans 5:10), so that they may become friends of God. For it is plainly said that Jesus took all things upon himself for sinners (Romans 5:8), that he might “set them free” from sin (Hebrews 2:15) and make them “righteous” (Romans 5:19).

choices.choice: 'no mere appearance' -> 'no semblance' ('mere' was an addition to οὐ δόκησιν)

'What absurdity is there, then, if something of this kind took place when something of this kind was going to save?' -> 'What is absurd, then, in something of this kind having taken place, if something of this kind was going to bring salvation?' (conditional order fixed, repetition kept)

'turn characters of a certain sort more when they are spoken in the way of falsehood than in the way of truth' -> 'when spoken falsely rather than truthfully, turn certain characters back' (calque removed)
noted in translator_notes that Hebrews 2:15 is a verbal allusion only
checked Romans 5:8, 5:10, 5:19 and Hebrews 2:15; Celsus's repeated words kept in quotation marks

'οι᾿ δόκησιν' in the staged text is a typesetting error for 'οὐ δόκησιν'; translated as 'no semblance'. 'δόκησις' is the term later used of Docetism; rendered 'semblance'. The sentence 'καὶ γάρ τινες τῶν λόγων ... ἤπερ κατὰ τὸ ἀληθές' is awkward in the transmitted text (the 'than according to the truth' clause is cut off by a full stop after the physician comparison); construed as one comparison and rendered so. 'ἐπιστρέφουσιν' rendered 'turn ... back', the same verb as 'bring back' the lost sheep in 4.17. 'τὸ φίλον τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος' plays on Celsus's 'friends'; rendered 'which is dear to him'. 'when one is taking care to escape danger' is put in quotation marks because Origen repeats Celsus's words from 4.18. 'ὁ ἀπολογησάμενος' = whoever offers the defence 'on behalf of others' (the hypothetical answer Origen has just given). Scripture: 'still enemies ... friends' echoes Romans 5:10 (ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν); 'for sinners' Romans 5:8; 'ἀπαλλάξῃ' is the verb of Hebrews 2:15 (there release from slavery under fear of death; Origen applies it to sin); 'δικαίους' echoes Romans 5:19 (δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται). These are allusions marked by quotation in Koetschau, not verbatim citations.
